directive: Continuation into the new year of Valerius’s winter administration, the active raid inquiry, the estate’s commercial preparations, and the growing local and Roman correspondence around his educational activities.

events.title: THE NEW YEAR OPENS WITH A FULL REVIEW OF THE WINTER STORES
events.body: The estate stewards begin the new year by reviewing the stores remaining after the first month of winter distribution. Grain, fodder, and preserved provisions are counted separately at the principal holdings and compared with the records sent from the outlying estates. The review identifies no immediate crisis, but it shows that the winter draw has made careful scheduling necessary through the remaining cold weeks. Granary keepers are instructed to preserve the established reserve rather than release additional stores without a recorded request. Valerius receives the consolidated figures and asks that the next agricultural preparations be recorded alongside the storage reports. The review turns the winter provisioning system into the first major administrative task of the new year.

events.title: THE RAID INQUIRY REACHES ANOTHER STAGE OF CORRESPONDENCE
events.body: Valerius's prepared account is carried onward through the correspondence connected with Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer. The material sets out the sequence of the merchant testimony and the earlier statements already preserved by Valerius. Celer's representatives request clarification on two points concerning the timing of the evidence, keeping the inquiry focused on the records rather than introducing a new accusation. Valerius supplies the requested chronology from his existing notes and retains copies of the material sent onward. The exchange gives the inquiry a more orderly documentary record as the new year begins. Aulus Vettius remains a named intermediary in the existing chain of correspondence, without the record establishing any broader role for him.

events.title: WINTER MERCHANTS BEGIN ARRANGING THE NEXT LAKE-PORT CYCLE
events.body: Merchants who completed the December settlement begin arranging the next movement of goods through the lake-port. The work consists of contracts, storage reservations, weighing arrangements, and discussions over which cargoes can be moved once conditions become more favorable. No new harbor construction is undertaken, and the merchants do not yet begin a new major shipment. Estate administrators nevertheless record the commitments because they will determine how the existing warehouses are used when traffic increases. The warehouse workers inspect the available storage areas and mark space for incoming consignments. The preparations connect the completed December commercial cycle with the next phase of the estate's trade activity.

events.title: A FARMER'S PETITION REACHES VALERIUS THROUGH THE WINTER READINGS
events.body: A smallholder attending the winter reading brings a petition concerning a boundary and access dispute affecting several neighboring fields. The request reaches Valerius through the same local circle that has grown around the estate library, rather than through the Roman correspondence. The petitioner asks that the matter be heard before the next agricultural work begins, when the disputed access route will again be in regular use. Valerius receives the petition and has the relevant local records brought together for examination. No ruling is issued during the gathering, and neither side is declared to have prevailed. The petition nevertheless expands the practical role that the estate's growing public-facing activities are beginning to play in the surrounding community.

events.title: VETERANS REPAIR THE OUTLYING WINTER WATCH POST
events.body: Veterans and estate guards return to the damaged watch position identified in December and complete the repairs that could be made from existing estate materials. The shelter is reinforced and a replacement store of firewood is placed under cover. The work is carried out as maintenance of the existing watch system rather than as an expansion of the guard network. The repaired position is inspected before the guards resume the winter rotation. Estate stewards add the completed work to the maintenance register and note which materials will be needed before the next cold season. The repair closes the immediate maintenance issue while leaving the broader security organization unchanged.

events.title: MARCELLUS RECEIVES COPIED QUESTIONS FROM THE ESTATE READINGS
events.body: Copies of the questions gathered during the winter readings are sent into the correspondence associated with Marcus Claudius Marcellus. The material includes questions from workers and nearby readers rather than only from the established scholarly circle. Marcellus acknowledges the collection and identifies several passages that he would like to discuss with Valerius and his correspondents. The exchange remains scholarly and personal, without creating a formal political appointment. Valerius's scribes preserve a duplicate set so that the local readers can continue the discussion while the Roman correspondence develops. The movement of these questions gives the estate library a second, more distant audience at the beginning of the year.

events.title: THE ESTATES COMPLETE THEIR FIRST WINTER FIELD ASSESSMENT
events.body: The stewards complete the first field assessment of the new agricultural year, recording the condition of the land, storage areas, and equipment that will be needed when regular field work resumes. Workers identify several sections that will require additional preparation before planting, while the principal grain stores remain sufficient for the immediate winter period. The assessment does not change the size of Valerius's holdings, but it gives the administrators a more detailed starting point for the coming agricultural cycle. Valerius receives the report alongside the final winter storage figures. The combined record links the estate's winter consumption with the practical requirements of the next season. The January administration therefore closes with the agricultural operation prepared for the transition toward spring work.
